verdict.rationale: The evidence pack does not name any official first-party state management library for Angular. The only state-related evidence is the homepage tagline about fine-grained reactivity built on Angular Signals, which is a core reactivity primitive developers could use to build state management, not a dedicated library. The "first-party modules for forms, routing, and more" claim does not name state management.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official first-party state management library maintained alongside the framework
